newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany plans currency revaluation first - finmin.
newsitem.headline: Germany plans currency revaluation first - finmin.

text.p: Germany will likely proceed with a revaluation of Bundesbank currency reserves before reassessing the worth of the central bank's gold reserves, a Finance Ministry spokeswoman told a news briefing on Wednesday.
"To my knowledge, (Tuesday's agreement) relates initially to the currency reserves," the spokeswoman said.

Earlier, Finance Minister Theo Waigel had read to parliament a statement agreed between him and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer following discussions between the two on the controversial plan on Tuesday.

"There will be a serious attempt to seek a mutually acceptable solution that will permit a revaluation of certain assets in the year 1997 with a pay-out (of resulting profits) to take effect in 1998," Weigel said.
Bundesbank currency reserves are valued at around 78.9 billion dollars based on last available information. It has a further 95 million ounces of gold in reserves.
